newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First Maori MP says his voters favour Labour.
newsitem.headline: NZ First Maori MP says his voters favour Labour.

text.p: A Maori MP from the New Zealand First Party said on Tuesday his supporters wanted him to support a coalition deal with the Labour Party but he would be guided by the best interests of the country.
Tutekawa Wyllie, MP for the Southern Maori seat Te Tai Tonga, said there were still about half a dozen "grey areas" where he sought more clarity of detail.
He acknowledged his own constituency supporters favoured Labour as a coalition partner. "Yes, my people have an expectation of me to go Labour."
Wyllie said he would make the decision in the best interests of the country. Asked if that would be with Labour, he said: "It may well be."

New Zealand First won all five special Maori seats in the October general election. Maori, who traditionally have been aligned with Labour in New Zealand politics, exert a strong influence within the party.
Wyllie agreed the alternative coalition proposals from the National Party and Labour had some similarities.

NZ First holds the balance of power between the conservative National caretaker government and Labour, and its MPs were meeting to decide on their preferred coalition partner on Tuesday. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
